1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
3	# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
4	# name "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, state-diff) appear only under
5	# ANDESIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
6	# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
7	# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
8	# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
9	set -uo pipefail
10	
11	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
12	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
13	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
14	
15	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
16	
17	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
18	
19	# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
20	has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
21	no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }
22	
23	# 1. release --help: run + list + doctor, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
24	H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
25	has '^  run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
26	has '^  list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
27	has '^  doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'doctor'"
28	for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
29	  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
30	done
31	no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
32	has 'ANDESIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
33	ok "release --help: run/list/doctor, dev hint, no verilator"
34	
35	# 2. ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/state-diff; doctor still shows
36	# (now release-tier, always listed); the hidden five stay hidden.
37	D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
38	for c in run list doctor build test state-diff; do
39	  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
40	done
41	for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
42	  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
43	done
44	no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
45	ok "dev --help: adds build/test/state-diff, doctor still shown, hidden cmds hidden, no verilator"
46	
47	# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
48	# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc -- icount was
49	# removed, simpoint is unfinished).
50	RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
51	has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
52	no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
53	has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"
54	has 'trigger.*icount' "$RH" && fail "run --help: --trigger should not list removed 'icount':"$'\n'"$RH"
55	has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
56	has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
57	# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
58	has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
59	has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
60	has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
61	ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator/simpoint, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"
62	
63	# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
64	# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail, no unfinished trigger.
65	LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
66	has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
67	no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
68	for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset' 'simpoint' 'icount'; do
69	  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail/removed-or-unfinished trigger '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
70	done
71	ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail, no simpoint/icount"
72	
73	# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
74	# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
75	# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
76	TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
77	cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
78	#!/bin/sh
79	[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
80	EOF
81	chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
82	LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
83	has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
84	no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
85	# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
86	# carries no TRIGGERS column (and so never leaks the unfinished simpoint trigger
87	# that the built-in qemu row used to advertise).
88	has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
89	has 'simpoint'  "$LE" && fail "list engines: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$LE"
90	ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"
91	
92	# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
93	# workloads): release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it.
94	printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release --help: leaked 'fixtures' target"
95	LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
96	printf '%s\n' "$LH" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures':"$'\n'"$LH"
97	has 'models' "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
98	expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
99	DLH=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
100	printf '%s\n' "$DLH" | grep -qw fixtures || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
101	ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
102	ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it)"
103	
104	ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

1	# Switching-Mode Tutorial and Exercises
2	
3	Status: draft for review
4	Audience: engineer running the hybrid co-simulator for the first time
5	Scope: the 4 switching modes the repo ships, with copy-paste commands,
6	the cycle figure each one yields, and one exercise per mode.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 0. What "switching mode" means
11	
12	The hybrid simulator runs a program across two phases:
13	
14	```
15	   QEMU1  --(state file + shared mmap)-->  vsim
16	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
17	```
18	
19	A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN QEMU1 drains its
20	architectural state and hands the region of interest to vsim. vsim runs
21	that region cycle-accurately, then drains the final state. You pick
22	the rule with plugin args and vsim CLI flags; the fixture binary does not
23	have to change between modes.
24	
25	> **Two ways to invoke, one canonical.** `./andesim run` is the driver -
26	> the supported way to run a workload, and what the examples below lead
27	> with. `tests/e2e.sh` is the regression harness that wraps the same legs
28	> behind `FIXTURE=... TRIGGER_MODE=... bash tests/e2e.sh`; it adds test-only
29	> assertions (`CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC`, `EXPECT_RC`, ...) and is shown only
30	> where those diagnostics are the point. When in doubt, use `./andesim run`.
31	
32	The repo ships **4 modes**, split by WHAT you profile.
33	
34	### Quick map
35	
36	| # | Mode | Profiles | Switch boundary | Cycle figure it yields |
37	|---|------|----------|-----------------|------------------------|
38	| 1 | marker | a kernel | `slti x0,x0,0x5A0` (enter) / `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` (exit) | kernel cycles |
39	| 2 | PC | a kernel | a PC / symbol address (no source edit) | kernel cycles |
40	| 3 | icount | a sampled window | N retired insns (single boundary) | window cycles |
41	| 4 | SimPoint | the whole program | clustering picks representative slices | whole-program estimate |
42	
43	- **Kernel modes (marker, PC)** measure ONE region you choose.
44	- **Whole-program modes (icount, SimPoint)** sample by instruction count.
45	  icount measures one window you place by hand; SimPoint measures several
46	  representative windows that clustering picks for you, then weight-combines
47	  them into a whole-program estimate. **SimPoint is just icount repeated.**
48	
49	(Migration: the old M1-M8 list collapses to these 4. Old M4-M7 are now
50	SimPoint stages; old M8 - the QEMU2 semihosting exit - was removed with
51	the QEMU2 phase, so every run now ends at the vsim drain.)
52	
53	### Where the cycle figure comes from
54	
55	Every mode reads the same counter: `mcycle`, a little-endian `uint64` at
56	byte offset **624** in the state file (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`). vsim
57	restores `mcycle` from QEMU1's drained value, then the RTL counts real
58	clock cycles, so the measured cycles are always a subtraction:
59	
60	```
61	cycles = mcycle(vsim drain) - mcycle(QEMU1 drain)
62	```
63	
64	The QEMU baseline cancels; only vsim's cycle-accurate delta survives. That
65	is why QEMU being functional-only (not cycle-accurate) does not taint the
66	number. marker/pc/icount report this delta directly (kernel / window cycles);
67	SimPoint extrapolates many such deltas into a whole-program estimate
68	(Section 5).
69	
70	---
71	
72	## 1. One-time prerequisites
73	
74	Build everything once. Each command is idempotent.
75	
76	```sh
77	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
78	source ./setup.sh         # qemu + vsim + plugin + simpoint
79	```
80	
81	You should now have:
82	
83	| Artifact                                | Purpose                           |
84	|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
85	| `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`        | QEMU binary (phase 1)             |
86	| `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium`   | vsim binary (phase 2)             |
87	| `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`      | TCG plugin (state drainer)        |
88	| `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`           | SimPoint clustering tool (mode 4) |
89	| `tests/fixtures/*.elf`                  | Test fixtures (e.g. rt_c_v_matmul) |
90	
91	Common env vars (auto-detected by `./andesim` and the e2e harness;
92	override only if you keep these elsewhere):
93	
94	```sh
95	export VSIM_QEMU=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
96	export VSIM_PLUGIN=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
97	export VSIM_BIN=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium
98	```
99	
100	---
101	
102	## 2. marker mode - the default (profiles a kernel)
103	
104	### What it does
105	
106	QEMU1's plugin pattern-matches the encoding `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` at retire
107	time. On hit it drains state to `outfile` and exits 200. vsim does the
108	same on `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`. The markers are RISC-V HINT NOPs (rd=x0), safe on every
109	core, so the fixture binary embeds these two `slti` instructions at the
110	kernel boundaries. vsim's drain at the `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` marker is the
111	natural tail of the run.
112	
113	### Inputs
114	
115	- Fixture ELF with `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` and `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` in its source.
116	  Every C-level fixture (rt_c_v_matmul, rt_c_v_regs, rt_c_matmul, etc.) has these.
117	
118	### Cycle figure
119	
120	Kernel cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta over the region between the two
121	markers. Run with `CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1` and the harness prints
122	`mcycle` at both ends:
123	
124	```sh
125	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=marker CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1 TIMEOUT=120 \
126	  bash tests/e2e.sh
127	```
128	
129	Look for the two lines `qemu1: mcycle=...` and `vsim: mcycle=...`; the
130	kernel cycle count is `vsim - qemu1` (the GEMM kernel is ~22808 cycles).
131	
132	### Run it
133	
134	```sh
135	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
136	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium
137	```
138	
139	`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker` orchestrates the QEMU1 → vsim handoff directly (driver/cmd_run.cpp). Before the final PASS line it prints the cycle figure:
140	
141	```
142	[marker window_cycles] 22808  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
143	PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_v_matmul)
144	```
145	
146	The plugin gets `outfile=<state.bin>` and nothing else - that is the marker
147	default. vsim is launched without `--hybrid-exit-pc` and without
148	`--hybrid-icount`, so its ELF pre-scanner watches for `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` PCs
149	at retire.
150	
151	### Exercise 1
152	
153	The `./andesim run` examples default to the GEMM, but the harness is
154	fixture-parameterized - switch from `rt_c_v_matmul` to `rt_c_matmul`
155	(a scalar matmul) to confirm:
156

file.content:
# Build the user-facing andesim runtime library into build/runtime/:
#
#   libandesim_runtime.a   trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o
#   crt0.o                   startfile; kept OUTSIDE the archive because
#                            nothing references _start, so the linker
#                            would never extract it from a .a (same
#                            reason toolchains ship crt0.o next to libc.a)
#   andesim.ld             linker script (load base 0x00100000)
#   include/andesim/ROI.h  ROI markers (HINT NOPs; same dir rides -B)
#
# Users link with:
#   gcc ... -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c
# or, without the gcc driver:
#   gcc ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T andesim.ld crt0.o hello.c \
#       -L <repo>/build/runtime \
#       -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
#
# Toolchain location comes from config.env (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN), same as
# tests/fixtures/Makefile.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
AR := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ar

OUT ?= ../build/runtime

# rv64gc objects link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the RISC-V
# arch attributes), so one build serves both -march variants.
CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

LIB_OBJS := $(OUT)/trap.o $(OUT)/handler.o $(OUT)/vplat_syscalls.o

.PHONY: all clean

all: $(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a $(OUT)/crt0.o $(OUT)/andesim.ld \
     $(OUT)/andesim.specs $(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.S | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.c | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/trap.o: core_v5.h

$(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a: $(LIB_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

$(OUT)/andesim.ld: andesim.ld | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

$(OUT)/andesim.specs: andesim.specs | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

# gcc adds <-B prefix>/include to the include path, so the two-flag user
# command resolves #include <andesim/ROI.h> with no extra -I.
$(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h: ROI.h | $(OUT)
	mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	cp $< $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(OUT)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# andesim: repo-root entry for the C++ driver (build/andesim).
# Self-bootstraps on first use so a fresh clone can run ./andesim
# directly; the build is host-only (no Verilator/SystemC/QEMU needed).
#
# macOS is run-only: both legs must share one Linux kernel, so the wrapper
# re-execs inside the prebuilt runtime image (podman machine VM); the shared
# mmap then lives in the VM, never on a virtiofs mount. ANDESIM_OS is a
# test hook to force the branch from Linux.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

if [ "${ANDESIM_OS:-$(uname -s)}" = "Darwin" ]; then
  exec bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_in_container.sh" "$@"
fi

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >&2
exec "$BIN" "$@"

## Code-quality review (altitude angle) -- uncommitted diff in `driver/ runtime/ tests/`

Verdict up front: the substantive (non-rename) changes are almost all at the right altitude. The icount removal was done cleanly at the user-facing layer while preserving the internal `icount` plan mechanism, and `doctor`'s tier move uses the existing mechanism with no special-case. Two findings worth surfacing: one concrete bug (help-column misalignment caused by the rename), and a clear recommendation on the now-dead defensive guards.

---

### Finding 1 -- `driver/main.cpp:104` -- `--mode` help line is misaligned by one column
- Summary: the renamed `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` line's description starts at column 36; every other flag in the same block (including the newly added `--gdb`/`--gdb-port`) starts at column 37.
- Why the depth is wrong: this is the rename leaking into output the task said should stay clean. `--model` was one char longer than `--mode`; when the author shortened the flag they did not add a compensating space, so the description column lost alignment for exactly that one row. The new `--gdb` lines were added at the correct col 37, which makes the stray row visibly crooked in `run --help`.
- Deeper fix: add one space after `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` so its description aligns at col 37 with the rest. (Purely cosmetic, but it is user-facing release help and the diff itself introduced the inconsistency.)

### Finding 2 -- `driver/main.cpp:112-115` -- `--gdb`/`--gdb-port` placement is correct
- Summary: the two new help lines sit in the always-printed release `std::fputs` block (before the `if (is_dev_mode())` dev block), matching `Cli::gdb` being a release-tier flag valid on fast/cycle.
- Assessment: right altitude. `--gdb` is a user-facing debugging entry (it has its own release-surface test assertions in `test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh:622-623`), so documenting it in the release block - not the dev block - is consistent with how `--verify` and `--mem-size` are documented, and inconsistent placement (dev block) would have under-advertised a shipped feature. No change needed.

### Finding 3 -- `driver/cmd_run.cpp:444-445` and `:448-449` -- the `--verify`/`--cosim` "supports --trigger marker|pc" guards are now dead AND untested
- Summary: after `hybrid_trigger()` returns with `err.empty()`, `trig.kind` is provably `"marker"` or `"pc"` (every other branch in `hybrid.cpp` sets `err` and returns empty kind; simpoint errors at `hybrid.cpp:32`). So both `trig.kind != "marker" && trig.kind != "pc"` conditions are always false.
- Why this depth is now wrong: these were meaningful guards when `icount` was a valid trigger that the cosim/verify legs could not arm on. With `icount` gone they guard nothing reachable, and - critically - the one test that exercised them (the `expect 2 'cosim supports --trigger marker\|pc'` case with `--trigger icount` in `test_andes_sim_cosim.sh`) was deleted in this same diff. `cmd_run.cpp` is compiled only into the `andesim` binary, not into any unit-test target, so there is now no automated coverage of these two error strings at all. A "defensive invariant" that is both unreachable and untested is dead weight: it cannot regress-test anything, and a future reader has to re-derive that it is unreachable.
- Recommendation (clear): remove both guards (lines 444-445 and 448-449, with their comments). The invariant they protect - "a hybrid trigger is always marker or pc" - belongs at its source, `hybrid_trigger()`, which already enforces it by construction and IS unit-tested (`hybrid_test.cpp` checks the simpoint/icount/bogus error paths directly). If you want the invariant stated for future readers, a one-line comment or an `assert(trig.kind == "marker" || trig.kind == "pc")` documents it without pretending to be a tested user-facing error path. Keeping the current `return fail(...)` form is the worse altitude: it dresses up a structurally-impossible state as a recoverable CLI error.

### Finding 4 -- `driver/hybrid.cpp:55-58` -- the kanata "marker or pc" guard is also CLI-unreachable, but this one should STAY
- Summary: the live caller (`cmd_run.cpp:460`) passes `trig.kind`, again provably marker|pc, so the kanata error branch cannot fire from the CLI either.
- Why this is a different case from Finding 3: `vsim_extra_args()` is a small pure function that IS compiled into `andesim-hybrid-test` and is directly unit-tested with a non-marker/pc kind (`hybrid_test.cpp` now calls `vsim_extra_args(..., "simpoint", err)` and asserts the error). So unlike the cmd_run guards, this guard's behavior remains exercised and locked. Keeping it is the right altitude: it makes `vsim_extra_args` a self-contained, total function whose contract holds for any `kind` a future trigger might introduce, and the cost is one tested branch rather than an unverified dead one.
- Recommendation: keep as-is. (This is the consistent answer to the task's "is keeping unreachable guards worse than removing them" question: the discriminator is testability + locality, not reachability. The hybrid.cpp guard passes both; the cmd_run guards fail both.)

### Finding 5 -- user-facing `--trigger marker|pc` vs internal `icount` plan kind -- layering is coherent
- Summary: `hybrid.cpp` (the CLI->Trigger mapping) no longer emits an `icount` kind, while `plan.hpp`/`run_plan.cpp` retain the `icount` plan mechanism for SimPoint.
- Assessment: right altitude, and the split is well-marked. The seam is clean: `hybrid_trigger()` is the single chokepoint that decides which trigger kinds are user-selectable, and it simply stopped producing `icount`. The plan layer never knew about CLI surface - it consumes a `Trigger` with params - so leaving its icount path intact for the SimPoint pipeline does not leak any icount concept back to the user. The comment added at `hybrid_test.cpp` (the "measurement mechanism survives in the plan layer ... no longer CLI-selectable" note) documents exactly this boundary. No confusion; this is the textbook way to retire a user-facing option without ripping out infrastructure a sibling feature still needs.

### Finding 6 -- `Cli::model` field kept while flag is `--mode`; `tests/andes_sim/` + `namespace andes_sim` kept -- one minor concern
- Summary: the parse table maps `{"--mode", &c.model}` (`cli.cpp:76`); the struct field stays `model` with comment `// --mode fast|cycle|hybrid`.
- Assessment: the kept `model` field is fine and intentional - the "model" concept (`list models`, `find_model`, `models.hpp`, the `unknown model '...'` errors) is a real domain noun distinct from the `--mode` selector flag, so a flag-name change need not rename the concept. There are zero remaining user-facing `--model` literals in non-test driver source (verified), so nothing leaks. The internal-only `andes_sim` namespace and `tests/andes_sim/` dir are likewise invisible to users.
- The one concern: there is now a permanent flag-name/field-name mismatch (`--mode` -> `Cli::model`) plus a directory/namespace (`andes_sim`) that no longer matches the product name (`andesim`). This is a small, deliberate, documented inconsistency, not a defect - but it is exactly the kind of thing the next contributor will "helpfully" try to finish renaming. Recommendation: add a one-line note at the `Cli::model` declaration (e.g. `// field intentionally 'model': the --mode flag selects a *model*; concept name kept`) so the half-rename reads as a decision, not an oversight. No code change otherwise.

---

Out-of-scope note (not one of the 5 questions, flagging once): `cmd_run.cpp:run_cycle_gdb` also changed substantively beyond the rename - it drops vsim's `-S` and now execs ICEman with `-I virtual_dmi.cfg`. That cfg and the `interface/` dir it implies are present but untracked (`git status` shows `?? interface/`, `?? virtual_dmi.cfg`). If the `--gdb` cycle path is meant to work for other users, those need to be committed or generated; that is a provisioning concern separate from the rename review.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run --verify contract (verify_oracle F4): opt-in oracle cross-check.
#   1. hybrid marker --verify  -> oracle leg + "[verify] PASS", rc 0
#   2. hybrid pc --verify      -> same through the exit_pc oracle path
#   3. default (no --verify)   -> no verify leg, no verify output
#   4. --verify with fast/cycle -> usage error (rc 2)
#   5. --verify with icount     -> usage error (rc 2)
#   6. run --help documents --verify
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"

# 1. marker mode.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --verify \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker --verify rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[verify\] PASS' || fail "marker: no [verify] PASS: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[state-diff\] PASS' || fail "marker: no state-diff detail: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'window_cycles' || fail "marker: cycle figure missing: $OUT"
ok "hybrid marker --verify: oracle cross-check PASS"

# 2. pc mode (boundaries = the fixture's own marker PCs, like docs 4.2).
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
  || fail "no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"
OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENGINE" \
      --pc-start "0x${MARKERS%% *}" --pc-end "0x${MARKERS##* }" --verify \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc --verify rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[verify\] PASS' || fail "pc: no [verify] PASS: $OUT"
ok "hybrid pc --verify: oracle cross-check PASS"

# 3. default off: no oracle leg, no verify output.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "default hybrid rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -qi 'verify' && fail "default run leaked verify output: $OUT"
ok "default: verification stays off"

# 4 + 5. usage errors.
expect 2 'verify requires --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode fast --verify "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'verify requires --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode cycle --verify "$VSIM_ELF"
ok "--verify usage errors (fast/cycle)"

# 6. run --help documents the flag.
expect 0 ' --verify ' "$BIN" run --help
ok "run --help documents --verify"

ok "run --verify oracle cross-check"
